Bug: `PUT /api/v1/items/{id}` returns a 500 instead of a validation error when the body sets `title` to null.
- Repro: create an item, then `PUT /api/v1/items/{id}` with `{"title": null}`. `ItemUpdate` in `backend/app/models.py` accepts the null. `update_item` in `backend/app/api/routes/items.py` then copies it onto the row through `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` and `sqlmodel_update`, and the commit fails on the non-null `title` column.
- Same pattern in `PATCH /api/v1/users/{user_id}`: `UserUpdate` allows `email`, `is_active` and `is_superuser` to be null. `update_user` only checks `if user_in.email:` and `crud.update_user` writes the nulls through.
- Explicit nulls on non-nullable fields must be rejected with a 422 before anything reaches the session.
- `description` (items) and `full_name` (users) must stay clearable by sending null. This is a product decision; don't change it.
- The `ItemPublic` and `UserPublic` response models must stay unchanged.
Acceptance: new cases in `backend/tests/api/routes/test_items.py` and `backend/tests/api/routes/test_users.py` cover the null-title, null-email and cleared-description/full_name paths. All existing tests in `backend/tests/api/routes/` pass unchanged.

Bug: item totals returned by `POST /api/v1/items/` are off by a cent on roughly 3% of items.
- Repro: quantity 7.345, base 2.50, unit price 1.15 (the case in `backend/tests/api/routes/test_items.py`) returns 10.94 instead of 10.95
- Cause is likely float math in `compute_item_total` in `backend/app/crud.py` before the final `round()`
- Switch the whole calculation to `Decimal` with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, applied once at the end
- Tax and discount must be applied in that order (product decision, don't change it)
- The `ItemPublic` response model in `backend/app/models.py` should still serialize amounts as strings with 2 decimals
Acceptance: all total cases in `test_items.py` match the expected values, and the existing API tests in `backend/tests/api/routes/` pass unchanged.

text: In the frontend, any 403 from the API logs the user out. `handleApiError` in `frontend/src/main.tsx` clears `access_token` and redirects to `/login` for both 401 and 403. Ordinary permission errors therefore act like an expired session. One example is "Not enough permissions" from the items routes. Another is a superuser hitting Delete in `frontend/src/components/UserSettings/DeleteConfirmation.tsx`, which gets "Super users are not allowed to delete themselves". In both cases the user is kicked to the login page instead of seeing the error toast. The backend's real invalid-token case is the 403 with detail "Could not validate credentials" raised in `get_current_user` (`backend/app/api/deps.py`). Keep the diff minimal: only log out on 401 or on that specific credentials 403, and let every other 403 fall through to the existing `handleError` toast. Add no new packages, and don't touch the generated client in `frontend/src/client`.

Goal: add an importer that loads item records from partner export drops into the `item` table (`Item` in backend/app/models.py). None of this exists yet.
- Create a new package backend/app/importers/ with a CLI module `load_items.py`. It reads drops from `exports/items/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/*.json`, with the base directory taken from a `--source-dir` option. Each drop also contains a manifest.json with the per-partner item counts.
- Three partner systems write these files, and their field names differ slightly (`created` vs `created_at`, `owner_email` vs `user_email`). Put the field mapping in a new backend/app/importers/mappings.py, one dict per partner.
- Normalize `created_at` to UTC. One partner writes local time. For its files, use per-partner offsets from a new backend/app/importers/partner_timezones.csv.
- Resolve `owner_id` from the email with `crud.get_user_by_email`.
- Dedupe on (owner_id, title, created_at) before insert.
- The load must be idempotent: rerunning a date replaces the items loaded from that date's drop and never appends.
- Add a small sample drop for 2026-10-20, with its manifest.json, so the command can be run.
Acceptance: running `uv run python -m app.importers.load_items --date 2026-10-20` from backend/ twice leaves the same row count in `item`, and the item count per partner matches that drop's manifest.json.

Acceptance: running `uv run python -m app.importers.load_items --date 2026-10-20` from backend/ twice leaves the same row count, and the item count per partner matches the manifest.json that ships with each drop.

text: Two kinds of JWT are signed with the same `SECRET_KEY` and `HS256`: access tokens from `create_access_token` in `backend/app/core/security.py`, and password-reset tokens from `generate_password_reset_token` in `backend/app/utils.py`. Neither carries a token-type claim. As a result, each kind decodes successfully wherever the other is expected, and only the `sub` lookup happens to fail. Please harden this: add a type claim to both, and make `get_current_user` in `backend/app/api/deps.py` and `verify_password_reset_token` reject tokens of the wrong type. Keep the diff minimal and don't change any function signatures, because the routes in `login.py` and `users.py` and the helpers in `backend/tests/utils/` call them by name.

text: Users with more than 100 items only ever see their newest 100 on the Items page, and the admin page stops at 100 users. `getItemsQueryOptions` in `frontend/src/routes/_layout/items.tsx` always calls `ItemsService.readItems` with `skip: 0, limit: 100`, and `getUsersQueryOptions` in `frontend/src/routes/_layout/admin.tsx` does the same with `UsersService.readUsers`. `DataTable` in `frontend/src/components/Common/DataTable.tsx` then paginates only that first slice on the client and ignores the `count` that `read_items` and `read_users` in `backend/app/api/routes/` already return. Its "of N entries" text and page count are built from `data.length`, so anything past 100 never appears. Can you fix this so paging through the tables reaches every item and user exactly once, using `skip`/`limit` and the returned `count`?
